utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. The late sitting of the previous trial has caused us to have to commence later this afternoon; I'm sorry about that. And while mentioning that delay in our programme, could the Chamber mention that next Wednesday, it will be unable to sit as programmed, because of the need to allow another trial to proceed. We simply don't have enough courtrooms to go around at the moment. So if you can take that into account as you look at your programming of next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It may be two weeks, not next week; I'm being reminded that I'm getting ahead of myself. It's a good thing there's three Judges, not one. Now Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. As the Chamber may recall, on the 20th of June of this year, there was a discussion about several pending Prosecution motions seeking leave to drop certain witnesses from the Prosecution's list, Rule 65 ter list, of witnesses. And on that day specifically, with respect to the Prosecution's fifth motion to withdraw certain witnesses, there was a discussion, there were some comments with respect to Mr. Peter Matthiesen and the Prosecution -- excuse me, the Trial Chamber indicated that at that time would not make a final decision as to whether to granted Prosecution's motion with respect to Mr. Matthiesen; rather, the Trial Chamber preferred to wait until after the testimony of Mr. Hutsch was finished and then perhaps the parties could revisit the matter. Since the end of Mr. Hutsch's testimony, the Prosecution has spoken with Mr. Apostolski, because it was really -- it was the Defence for Mr. Tarculovski that in June opposed the Prosecution's motion on this point. And Mr. Apostolski has informed the Prosecution that the Tarculovski Defence will no longer oppose the Prosecution's request to have Mr. Matthiesen removed from its witness list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon. I see Mr. Apostolski's agreement with that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon Your Honour. I can only confirm what has been said by my learned colleague Dan Saxon. So regarding the witness, we have no special stance and we would leave to the Chamber to decide upon it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The -- Mr. Saxon, the Chamber would therefore, in respect of your fifth motion, grant leave for the withdrawal of the name of Mr. Matthiesen from the list of witnesses. Good afternoon, Mr. Bezruchenko. I'm sorry you have been kept waiting this long.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: May I remind you of your affirmation which still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And I expect that Mr. Mettraux still has a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The suspicion is accurate, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good afternoon Mr. Bezruchenko. Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown exhibit P232, please. It's under seal. Mr. Bezruchenko, you will recall the document. This is the same document as I was showing to you yesterday when we left off. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that you've indicated that you weren't certain whether you had or hadn't seen this particular document, but you recall having seen similar document relating to receipt for guns and ammunition. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, sir. I recall saying that I did not remember if I saw this specific document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you aware from the evidence of a witness called M-54 that this document had been prepared by this witness. Is that something within your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not really.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware, Mr. Bezruchenko, whether your office, and your colleagues made any effort to verify whether the individuals which are mentioned by names in this particular document as having received weapons in the Cair police station on the 11th of August had in fact become de jure members of the MOI? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D554.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What will appear on your screen, Mr. Bezruchenko, is a letter sent by the Defence of Mr. Boskoski to the Macedonian authorities asking them to verify the names of -- well, I'm sorry, to verify in relation to the name of a number of people whether the people in question have been receiving salary from the MOI during the period 1st August to 30 September 2001. Can you see that on the letter?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that, sir, but frankly speaking, I don't quite understand what is the relation between this document and my report, since A, none of the names, as I can see here, are mentioned in my report; and, B, as I mentioned previously, none of the crimes committed in Ljuboten were in fact described in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Saxon is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, unless Mr. Mettraux can show that this document or this line of questioning is somehow relevant to the credibility of Mr. Bezruchenko, the Prosecution does not understand what the relevance of this document or this line of questioning is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, we believe it's relevant to a number of things. The first one is indeed a issue of credibility of the witness. You will recall, Your Honour, that this particular witness has raised issues pertaining to the need for verification of the fact that a number of individuals believed by the Office of the Prosecutor to have partaken in the alleged crimes in and around Ljuboten were or weren't members of the MOI. The question I'm asking in relation to this, the other issue we believe is relevant is that in his report Mr. Bezruchenko is not limiting his evidence despite what has been claimed only to issues pertaining to the armed conflict but he is seeking to give evidence, inter alia, in relation to matters of disciplinary measures which Mr. Bezruchenko claims Mr. Boskoski had at the time, a pre-condition of the relevance of that very evidence, Your Honour, is the fact that the individual in question must have been members of -- de jure members of the MOI at the time. Mr. Bezruchenko knew from the analysis which is made of Mr. Boskoski book that at least there were some serious doubt as to whether that was the case or not. What the Defence is pursuing in this matter are those lines and in particular the fact that at some stage the Prosecution appear to have changed, so to say, its tack on the case and that the verification of whether or not these peoples who they claim were part of the MOI have ceased to be verified and that they have adopted in its place a theory of operational control and other theories which are to be found in Mr. Bezruchenko's report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: All of that is very interesting, in particular as part of a final address, Mr. Mettraux, but it really is straining relevance to this witness and his report, because you're going into matters which he has not dealt with, which he has not taken into account. If you're simply wanting to have it confirmed that he didn't take certain things into account because he didn't know about it, fine, but that's not what you're doing. You're going much beyond that. And you're really trying, as it were, to establish the contrary of a proposition by looking at facts and issues that have not been considered by the witness at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, in that case, I will move on from this particular question. As indicated to you, the belief of the Defence as to the particular relevance of this question was that a number of propositions are being made in the report, which, in effect, are contrary to the factual basis or part of the factual basis which was known to Mr. Bezruchenko, but I will comply with Your Honour's indication in relation to this since the witness has indicated that he had no knowledge of this particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, simply a matter related to this one but one which I hope you are aware of. Is that correct you as you reviewed the evidence which was given as part of these proceeding, you became aware of the fact that the -- the fact that a person received a weapon and ammunition from the police or from the MOI would not per se be sufficient to -- for this person to be regarded as a de jure member of the police. Are you aware of that evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think this evidence is reflected in my report, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for this indication. But the first question, Mr. Bezruchenko, was whether you were aware of the evidence in question.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you kindly reformulate your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Certainly. Are you aware that -- and I will perhaps give you the exact date which may assist you. Are you aware that on the 13 of June of 2007 evidence was given by a Prosecutor witness to the effect that the fact that a person would have been given gun and ammunition by the police would not be sufficient for him or her to become a de jure reserve policeman or woman. Are you aware of that evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would perhaps split my answer in two specific points. Well, I don't recall any such evidence specifically related to 13 June 2007. This is one thing. And the second thing, as a matter of general comment but not necessarily related to this specific situation and this specific case I would say that normally it doesn't suffice for a person with a weapon to be a member of any official organisation, for that matter, Ministry of Interior as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that. Your Honour, simply for the record, it is the evidence of M-053 the 13th of June 2007 at page 1971. Is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that in your report, the report which you've submitted in these proceedings, you make a number of references to so-called special units of the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that in the course of the investigation carried out by your office you received information from the Macedonian authorities that neither the Tiger units nor the Lions unit had been involved in the events in Ljuboten. Are you aware of that information?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then I would like you to turn your attention, once again, to what is P466, exhibit P466. It's again your report, Mr. Bezruchenko, and I will ask you to turn, please, to page 103 of the report. Perhaps to assist you, Mr. Bezruchenko, that would be one of the two charts which is included in your report. Can you locate it?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the title of that document it indicates that it is a chart of the Ministry of Interior and there's a date, August 2001. The first thing I would like to ask you is: Who prepared that particular chart, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you prepare it with the assistance of any other members of the team of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, in technical matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And when you referred to the date on the top left-hand corner or that would be the bottom left, depending how you look at it, to August 2001, what date in particular, if any, were you referring to, Mr. Bezruchenko, in the month of August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: End of August 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So that would be -- would it be correct to suggest that this would be after the 21st of August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that would be a chart that would be relevant, simply for the record, the 21st of August of 2001 is the date at which the new book of rule was adopted, is that correct, of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to specifically direct me to the specific document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. Bezruchenko. This would be Exhibit 1D66. Do you recognise that document, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page that may assist your memory as to the particular date of that document. Can you see the date at the bottom left of that document, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that would be the 21st of August of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And as you indicated before, was the chart that is included at page, I believe, 108 of your -- 103, I apologise, of your report based on these particular rules as amended?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And simply to look with you at those particular -- this particular amendment, rather, if you can turn your attention to Article 1 of the document, you will see that it refers to the fact that the special tasks unit Tiger from Article 7 is moved to the part, "department for police," in Article 4 and becomes item 6. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can turn to the next page, please, Mr. Bezruchenko, of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And for the registry as well, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can look down at the chart in question, in particular under the section "department for police." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you locate the special tasks unit Tiger within that department?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can see, this is -- was in the department of police and public safety bureau.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's what the previous page of the document said. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will agree also that the special tasks unit is separate from the sector for posebni or special unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it should be under the sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree that in fact, as this chart makes clear, it never became a part of the sector for special unit, contrary to what your chart suggest, but that it simply integrated in the department of police. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my interpretation of this diagram is slightly different, sir. Well, I don't really think that this is indeed the case. My interpretation of this diagram will be that in fact the three special police units were reporting indeed to the department of police but through the sector of special units.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that your interpretation is contrary to this diagram. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It is not contrary to the diagram which is present in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps we'll go back again to the previous page of this document. And if you look at the first or the last sentence of Article 1 it says that it becomes the unit Tiger from Article 7 is moved to part A, department for police in Article 4 and becomes item 6. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps to assist --

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please come back to this chart for a moment again.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This would be the next page, please, for Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps to assist you further, Mr. Bezruchenko, we can go back to the original or the previous version of the book of rules. Those were dated January of 2001, and that would be Exhibit 1D107, please. Do you recognise that document, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will recall that the previous document mentioned that the Tigers unit was moved from Article 7 to Article 4 and becomes item 6. So if we can go to Article 7 first of that initial version. It's at page 1D00-4399. And if you look at this Article, Mr. Bezruchenko, it says this: "Organisational forms that conduct determined expert work at the public security bureau and for the office security and counter-intelligence are, one, special tasks unit Tiger is a uniformed unit of the ministry which is under direct management and command of the minister. The minister with the special act may authorise the head of the department who manage the department for police to conduct affairs to enable, organise, exercise activities and other organisational issues in connection with the work of the unit." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir, are you referring specifically to Article 6?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It would be Article 7, I apologise if you don't have it on your screen, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the Macedonian version of Article 7 also be placed in front of Mr. Bezruchenko, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you see, Mr. Bezruchenko, the introductory sentence followed by paragraph 1 of that article which refer to the Tiger unit. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn now to what is page 1D00-4414. It would be 1D00-4414, please. Thank you very much. Mr. Bezruchenko, can you now locate where the Tigers unit was in the initial rule book. Can you see where it is on the chart?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean on the right side of the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: On either the Macedonian or the English. Are you able to locate the special task unit Tiger?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think it is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps it is --

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the sector for special units here.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if you look on the top right-hand corner, the second from the top under the security and counter-intelligence administration head. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you confirm that as indicated under Article 7 of this rule book the -- at the time in January 2001 and according to that regulation, the special tasks unit Tiger had three links, institutional link. One was to the minister, one to the public safety bureau and one to the security and counter-intelligence administration head. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you could somehow adjust this diagram on the screen, because I am' afraid it is not really fitting properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you able to locate --

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see this unit now. Well, in fact as far as I can see from this diagram, there is a direct link between this unit and the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I don't really think that there is a direct link, as you are suggesting, between this unit and the security and counter-intelligence administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree that these pointed and half-drawn lines also indicate, according to the rule book of the ministry that there were relations or links to the counter-intelligence and, as mentioned by Article 7, the public safety bureau. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would agree that in fact all those organisational elements and they are one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, which are directly under the special task unit Tiger were in fact the elements which were providing services to the security and counter-intelligence administration while -- but not necessarily perhaps being directly responsible to this administration because by -- simply by virtue of their services, they were supposed to provide service for the entire ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And looking perhaps one column to the left, Mr. Bezruchenko, do you agree that already at the time in the rule book of January of 2001 the sector for posebni or sometimes called sector for special units was already within the bureau for public safety under the head of the department for police. Can you locate that sector?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I read correctly, and this is a very small font, well, the last box on this right vertical line is sector for posebna units.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko --

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a bit strange because this is a mix of Macedonian and English.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you agree that this particular sector comes under the department for police. Do you agree with that it?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It Would appear that it would come under the public safety or security bureau.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And within that bureau it would come within the department of police. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would appear from this diagram, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we may turn back somewhat in this very document to page 1D00-4393, you will recall that the previous document that I showed you, the rule book of 21st of August of 2001, referred to the fact that the Tigers were moved on the 21st of August to Article 4. And I would like to show you what Article 4 is. And it's at the bottom of the page, please. Can you see Article 4, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this is, you will agree, a section which relates to the department for police. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you may turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And can we please ask the counsel and the witness not to overlap.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, do you agree that this Article 4 says the following. This is the second sentence. It says: "The police are composed of the following organisational forms?" Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you are specifically referring to Article 4, sir, I'm afraid not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I should help you. You see there's a first paragraph as a whole. Can you see that? Which started with the word: "The police implement." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the next sentence after this paragraph, there's another: "The police" in capital letters. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police are composed of the following --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- organisational units, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Bezruchenko. And it says this: "The police are composed of the following organisational forms." It says 1, duty operating centre; 2, sector for public peace and order; 3 sector for security in-road traffic; 4, sector for border crossing; and then there's 5, sector for special units which is composed of the centre for animal training and training, if we can go to the bottom of the page, please. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And now we can perhaps go back to the next document which I showed you a moment ago, which is Exhibit 1D66, please. And if we can turn to the next page again, please. Mr. Bezruchenko, that's the same rule book that I showed you a moment ago from the 21st of August of 2001 which amend the previous version. And if you look once again at this last sentence of Article 1 you will see that the unit special tasks unit Tiger is moved from Article 7, which I have read to you, to the part "a department for police in Article 4 and becomes item 6." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So do you agree that on the basis of what I have just shown you, the Tiger unit came or became part of the department for police on the 21st of August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not entirely certain if this can be interpreted this way, sir. You also recall there was another decision made by the president of the country as well as by Mr. Boskoski as well regarding the incorporation of certain special police units into the so-called temporary unit or as a provisional unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's stick with the Tigers Mr. --

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- Mr. Bezruchenko, let's stay with the Tigers for a moment. We will look later at the issue of the other unit which you have mentioned. But do you agree that at that stage the Tigers unit was placed not -- or was placed, rather, within the department for police but not within the special -- the sector for special or posebna unit but as an independent sector within that department. Do you agree that's what the document says?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would appear so, sir, but it would probably require additional analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree also that -- and perhaps I should show you the next page on that document again. This is page 1D00-2409. Do you agree that perhaps if it can shall -- yes. At this point in time on the 21st of August of 2001 do you agree that the unit which will later come to be known as the Lion units does not yet appear on this diagram. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the reason for it, I'm sure you will agree, is that these changes which brought a new unit inside the make of the ministry took place or was adopted in early September of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any specific date, sir, but my general impression from reviewing the related and the relevant documents was that the unit which later received the name Lions was fully operational and fully formed sometime by November 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But simply -- I'm grateful for that, Mr. Bezruchenko. But simply in relation to the structural issues and the location of the particular unit -- and instead of asking you off the top of your head, I will show you what is Exhibit 1D61; that may assist you. Mr. Bezruchenko, those are translated in the English as the rules on amendment and additions to the rules on the organisation and work of the Ministry of Interior. It's dated Skopje, September 2001. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if one may turn to the next page, please. If you can look first at the bottom left-hand corner, it suggests that the date at which those amendments were adopted is the 5th of September of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can look at the Article 1 of that document. It refers to a number of -- the various editions, so to say, of the rules and the last one being the 21st of August of 2001 which we have seen a moment ago. And it says that "a new subsection 5.1 is hereby added" and states "5.1 lines rapid intervention battalion" and then it says "the previous subsection 5.1 is now subsection 5.2." Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with that, sir, but I don't quite see how this document is actually fitting in my report since I was describing the structure of the Ministry of Interior as it stood in August 2001 .

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And was it your view at the time in August 2001 that the Lions were part of the sector for special unit, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my view was that this unit was already in the process of being formed as the appropriate decisions had been taken sometime in June 2001, but I don't think that this unit was fully formed and fully operational in August 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful for this clarification in this case, Mr. Bezruchenko. That's -- we may move forward on this issue. Do you recall being asked a number of questions from Mr. Saxon and also making a number of statements in your report about what you claim was the command and control of the MOI. Do you recall making those comments?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps before starting with this particular issue with you, I'd like the registry to show you once again Rule 65 ter 1D724, please. Mr. Bezruchenko, you will recall this document from yesterday. This is your summary and analysis of 24th April 2004. And if we can turn to page 18 of that document. That would be page 1D00-6428, please. And I'd like you to turn your mind again to paragraph 3, Mr. Bezruchenko. That's the first paragraph on this page. And I will road out what you said there. "Throughout the Albanian-Macedonian conflict Boskoski displayed a strong hands-on approach which was manifested in his activities to raise special police units, frequent visits on the front line police units, as well as his direct involvement and control of combat operations of those units. In the process, he was exposed to risk to his life several times. This kind of behaviour and style of leadership reflect the attitude of a military commander who feels that he alone is in charge, assume responsibility for his actions and personally leads his troops into action." Do you agree that already in April of 2004, Mr. Bezruchenko, and before you became an expert for the Prosecution, you had pretty strong views and arrested views about what you thought the nature of Mr. Boskoski's control, as you call, and involvement was. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I ask you a question, Mr. Mettraux?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, please, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Have you actually read this document in its entirety?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I have, Mr. Bezruchenko, read those parts which are available in the English. At this stage I will ask to you answer my question, which was whether you agree that before you had sat to write a report as a expert on behalf of the Prosecution, you had already strong views and made very clear findings as what you believed was Mr. Boskoski's style of leadership, to use your terms, and the fact that he behaved like a military commander. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would say that this was the impression I picked up after having read this book in its entirety. Many pages of this book are actually describing the visits of Mr. Boskoski to the front. I think he describes no less than seven or eight incidents when he was personally involved in a very serious risk of his life, as he called, attempts on his life, which apparently took place during his visits to the front line, when he was with the troops and directing them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that what you have done in your report is essentially to mold those views which you held already in April 2004 into your expert report. Do you agree that's what you did?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not necessarily. I don't really think that I mentioned the name of Mr. Boskoski at all in relation to his presence in Ljuboten. I don't think so. What I am describing there is just his role as the minister of the interior; that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that, as I indicated earlier and as you confirmed in evidence and also in your report, you have referred on a number of occasion to what is known in the military doctrine as the principle of command and control, which is in local terminology none as rukovodjenje i komandovanje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it also correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that this expression is a military term which has a specific military meaning in military doctrine. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which one are you specifically referring to, sir, operational control or RiK?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: RiK.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is a military term.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And just for the transcript, RiK refers to command and control in the English language. Mr. Bezruchenko, as a matter of introduction, are aware of any precedent or any authority from your field of military expertise where this concept of command and control was used and made to apply to non-military body or organs? Are you aware of any such case?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could you indicate what case, please?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The whole history of the war in Bosnia is awash with examples of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But as a matter of doctrine, Mr. Bezruchenko, are you aware of any authority which would suggest that this in fact is the case?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was not really specifically exploring the issue of any authorities which would actually make any specific comments on this particular situation. As far as I know, with the exception perhaps of very few people, any special reports on this issue had been made. I don't think any special reports had been made.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that. You have also indicated yesterday and again briefly today that you had followed the proceedings with a view, inter alia, to update your amended report. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was following these proceedings, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you become aware, as you followed the proceedings, of evidence led in this courtroom that would contradict the suggestion made by you in your report that the principle of command and control, or RiK, would apply to the activities of the Ministry of Interior of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a number of witness statements which I imagine would indeed contradict my view.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you feel you should make reference to the statement or the evidence of this witness in your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, for the reasons which I explained previously, one of them being is that generally speaking, I was trying to avoid as much as possible any speculative statements and was trying to rely on documents which actually would provide hard evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you will agree, I hope, Mr. Bezruchenko, that where the evidence was believed to fit your theories, you indeed relied on the evidence given in this trial. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was not the principle and it was not the main criteria. Actually it was not criteria at all. In my work, I was trying to be completely objective and reflect the strong facts and the situation as it was, to the best of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware for instance, Mr. Bezruchenko, of evidence being led in this trial to the effect that the employees of the Ministry of Interior did not need any particular orders, whether from the ministry or from the minister, to conduct their work and duties. Are you aware of that evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'm afraid you will have to qualify your statement. I don't quite understand what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, my question is this, Mr. Bezruchenko, in the course of following the proceedings in this case and the evidence which was given by Prosecution witness and witnesses, did you become aware of the evidence of a witness who said in this courtroom that employees -- perhaps I will read it out to you. That employees in general of the Ministry of Interior did not need specific order or particular orders from the ministry or the minister of the interior to conduct their work and duties. Are you aware of any such evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, I believe just as a matter of general comment I would say that there is nothing contradictory in this statement because obviously, you know, any smooth running organisation, every person and every employee knows what his functions and responsibilities are and what he is supposed to do, but this is only a general statement which should apply to a generally acceptable and normal situation. There may be other situations which would require direct interference of authorities a level, two levels, three levels above.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, simply for the transcript, this is the evidence of Mr. Toskovski of the 29th of August, 2007.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Have you become aware in the course of -- of following the proceedings in this case of the evidence of another witness, witness M-056, who explained that an order in the police is not the same as an order in the army. Do you agree that evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which specific order would you mean, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the witness in question was asked more generally whether there was any difference, I apologise, between a order received in the military context and an order received in the context of the military of the interior [sic]. Are you aware of that evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you make a reference of that particular evidence or that particular statement anywhere in your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will agree that this would be a pretty significant piece of information if one were to seek to apply military doctrines and military ideas to a different setting. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not necessarily, sir. Well, in fact the major operational activities in this field were limited mostly to deployment and combat operations, whether this required deployment of special police units, taking the villages back while sweeping the terrain, isolating the NLA units and so on and so forth. So in this sense, I don't really thing that the essence of the orders would differ very much. So formally, even in the ways they were prepared and written and described, of course there could be differences.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then perhaps I should ask you whether you are you aware of the evidence of another Prosecution witness, a man of military background, who indicated in his evidence that apart from the army no other state organ functioned according to the military principle of subordination which you, Mr. Bezruchenko, mentioned as a criminal factor in relation to the command and control doctrine which you say applied to the MOI. Are you aware of that evidence, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you could refresh my memory and specifically tell me which unit you mean, I would probably recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the evidence perhaps to assist you was the evidence of Mr. Mitre Despodov of the 25th of June of 2007 and this would be at page 2605. Do you recall the evidence being given by Mr. Despodov on that point?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you make reference or did you take any account of this evidence when you prepared your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Despodov's statement was certainly very interesting for me and certainly was important in shaping my understanding of how the command and control system worked in the army of Macedonia. But I don't think that Mr. Despodov was sufficiently qualified to say how the command and control system worked in any other institution of the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So, your view, Mr. Bezruchenko, is that because you believed Mr. Despodov to be not sufficiently competent in this matter, you disregarded his evidence in so far as pertain to this particular issue. Is that --

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Realtime transcript read in error] As far as the army is concerned, he was absolutely and fully competent and in fact I had no reasons not to trust his statement. But as far as the Ministry of Interior and any other institutions as you mentioned he referred to are concerned, well, I don't really think I could take this statement on its face value.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Before we go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I believe perhaps our hard-working court reporter may have missed the words as far as the military is concerned at the very start of Mr. Bezruchenko's last answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I am grateful to Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But perhaps, Mr. Bezruchenko, you will remember the evidence of Mr. Galevski, General Galevski of the police. Do you recall Mr. Galevski giving evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall Mr. Galevski making the point in particular that the minister of the interior did not have the power to order the use of police forces in military or combat activities. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do think -- yes, I think I do. I think he said something like this, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it something that you felt you should refer to in your report and if so, have you done so?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that this would explain the fact that Mr. Boskoski or that you did not or were not able to refer to any combat order signed by Mr. Boskoski, is that correct, because he didn't have the power to order the use of police forces in military and combat activities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not certain, sir. The fact that the special police units were in fact committed into combat operations were involved in fighting on daily basis and Mr. Boskoski was frequently seen with these units on the front would lead me to believe that he was at least a part of the decision-making group in the Ministry of Interior, whereas operational decisions as to the use of these units were concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, my question will be this for you. Did you see any such order or indication of involvement of Mr. Boskoski in the decision-making process?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned previously, I did not see any orders apart from those which we already discussed signed by Mr. Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And those would be the orders, you call them the orders but which in fact are telegrams of redeployment. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are telegrams but they are also orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, simply for the record, the evidence of Mr. Galevski to which reference was made was transcript of the 18th of July of 2007.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, and perhaps I should go back for one second to what is Rule 65 ter 1D724 again. And if we can go back to page 18 once again, please. And if I may draw your attention this time on paragraph 5 of your analysis and I will read it out to you. You said this: "Boskoski admitted that he was in Ljuboten in the afternoon on 12 August on specific request of President Trajkovski and Prime Minister Georgievski. This admission presents a new and important angle of the investigation and possibly could provide exculpatory evidence. A decision should be made if the role of Prime Minister Georgievski in the chain of command should be explored in the course of investigation." Do you recall making that comment?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that the concept which you have relied upon of operational control and RiK, command and control, is in fact an intelligence device to go around the problem that legally and as far as the government is concerned, the control of the police was in the hands of the prime minister. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily, sir. Let me make a general comment first. If you recall on the very first day of my testimony, you asked me what my functions and responsibilities in the military analysis unit were, and I started giving my account of those functions and responsibilities but you actually interrupted me. Well, let me finish this account now. One of the functions of the [indiscernible] is in fact to provide senior individuals in a time of conflict, either in the context of the crimes committed or in the context of a specific time-period related to a conflict. That may include very senior people, including army commanders and ministers. So this is the first point, my first point to your question. My second point to your question actually as to what you describe as intelligent device, well, I don't really know what actually is there to believe that the concept of operational control is an intelligence device. The concept of operational control is a concept of operational control as it has been described in numerous military regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that in his book Mr. Boskoski indicates, as you summarized, that he had gone to Ljuboten or Ljubanci on the 12th of August of 2001 at the request or at the behest of the prime minister and the president of the republic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you read my report carefully, Mr. Mettraux, you have probably noted that I don't really mention the name of Mr. Boskoski in relation to his visit to Ljubanci or Ljuboten at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, for the time being I'm asking you, Mr. Bezruchenko, about this particular document which you have prepared on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor in your capacity as a military analyst, and the first question is whether you recall what is noted in this particular analysis, namely the fact that in his book Mr. Boskoski indicated that he had gone to Ljuboten or Ljubanci on the 12th of August of 2001, on behalf or at the behest of the president of the republic and the prime minister. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are referring specifically to this document which is on the screen now, this is an analytical document which is describing a certain source and book and which draws certain analytical conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct also that as indicated in your book, you suggest at the end of this particular paragraph, paragraph 5, that during interviews of senior military -- well, first you say that in the course of further investigation -- sorry. I have -- here it is. You say: "A decision should be made if the role of Prime Minister Georgievski in the chain of command should be explored in the course of investigation." Do you recall making that comment?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall also that at a later stage, some months later, the Office of the Prosecutor in fact went to interview the former prime minister, Mr. Ljubco Georgievski. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think such a interview was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D865, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recognise the record of the statement taken from Mr. Ljubco Georgievski, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if the registry could please turn to page 3 of that document. That would be 1D00-752, please. I'd ask you, Mr. Bezruchenko -- if this could be enlarged somewhat for the witness, please. Thank you. I'll ask you, Mr. Bezruchenko, to turn to paragraph 11 of this document. Mr. Georgievski, Ljubco said the following: "As was reading the material prior to coming here for interview I found that Ljuboten operation took place on Sunday of 12th of August 2001. What I remember from that day is that I arrived to my office at 11.00 a.m. or 11.30 a.m., since I had a habit of going to work little bit later on Sundays. Some of my associates informing me that OSCE representative were looking for me regarding some urgent matter. I did not pay special attention to that message because at the time the diplomatic corps was constantly contacting me during -- regarding urgent matters. Then the OSCE representatives spoke again with someone from my office and said that something bad was happening in Ljuboten. After the second call, I decided to contact the minister of the interior, Ljube Boskoski. This call I made somewhere between 12.00 p.m. and 1.30 p.m. Since I was in the office, I believe that I used stationary phone to make the call." Then if we can turn to the next paragraph, please. This is what Mr. Georgievski recounted: "When I called Mr. Boskoski, I told him about the inquiries OSCE made and I asked him what was happening in Ljuboten. I remember clearly that he was surprised when I asked him this question. He answered that he has no idea what was going on in Ljuboten. Then I asked him to check what happened in Ljuboten." And it says: "In the next couple of days when I spoke with the minister of the interior Ljube Boskoski about Ljuboten events, he mentioned that at approximately the same time when I called him on Sunday he received a phone call from president of Macedonia Boris Trajkovski, who asked him to go to Ljuboten personally and help in calming and resolving the situation." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall Mr. Georgievski in fact confirming the statement of Mr. Boskoski which he made in his book about the fact that he had been asked by the prime minister and the president to go to the village to calm things down?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct also that another person to whom the office, your office had talked to was Mr. Zlatko Keskovski who at the time was the head of the security of the president of the republic. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think such a statement was made, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in fact you had used that particular statement in your original version of your report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you can specifically indicate which the statement was related to, I could probably tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, for the time being, the statement that I would like you to consider, if you may, is in Rule 65 ter 1D526, please. It's 1D00-4772, if it is of any assistance. Mr. Bezruchenko, while the statement of Mr. Keskovski is reaching our screens, I will start reading the paragraph in question, which is relevant here. It would be at page 11, please, of the statement, and that would be page 1D00-4782. And if we could focus, please, on paragraph 52. I'll read this paragraph for you, Mr. Bezruchenko. It says this, Mr. Keskovski is talking about phone call which he is making and he said: "I explained the driver that the president wanted to spoke to the minister. The driver put Ljube Boskoski on the phone and gave the phone to the president. I do not remember from which phone I was calling. I know what the president was saying but I did not hear the answers of Ljube Boskoski. The president informed Boskoski about the difficult situation in Radisani and asked him if he knew anything else about what was happening there. The president told Boskoski to go there personally and calm down the situation because it was important to sign Ohrid Agreement. The president also told Boskoski to call him later and inform him about the situation." Do you recall reading that particular paragraph of the statement of Mr. Keskovski as you were reviewing the material, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I read this paragraph, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that, again, this statement or the information provided by Mr. Keskovski confirms the information contained in Mr. Boskoski's book to the effect that he went to the village at the behest of, in this case, the president. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this paragraph basically confers with what I have seen in the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree that -- and you have indicated yesterday, I believe, that as part of the interviews which you've taken part in, you have interviewed the -- Mr. Vlado Buckovski who in 2001 for part of the year and at the time relevant to the charges was the minister of defence of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was involved in this interview, but I wouldn't say I really interviewed the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall now, Mr. Bezruchenko, that in the course of that meeting Mr. Buckovski, the minister of defence, had made it clear to you the police forces of the Ministry of Interior were under the control of the prime minister, Mr. Georgievski. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that he said something to this effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that that particular phrase or that particular statement made by the then-minister of defence, you had referred to in the original version of your report at paragraph 401. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a second, sir. Well, I think the exact phrase as it's -- it was present in the previous version of the report was "however, according to minister of Defence Boskoski this idea never worked and the unit was never created because Georgievski wanted to keep control of police in his hands." This is what I said previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that this sentence which you have read has been removed from the amended version of your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient time, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We adjourn to resume in half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, I'd like to make a parentheses at this stage. Do you recall that yesterday I suggested to you that the reason why you had been selected to be the expert by the Office of the Prosecutor was not because of your expertise but because you shared the views of the OTP team. Do you recall me putting that proposition in slightly different terms to you yesterday?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall your questions and I think my answer was basically no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that you were asked to prepare a so-called expert report sometimes between the late summer of 2005 and the early Autumn of 2005. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure, but that may have been 2004 as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that on the 7th of November of 2005 you appeared on the Rule 65 ter list as a proposed expert witness. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was not really working on this specific list, but indeed there was an opportunity for me to appear on this list, as I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've indicated, I believe in your evidence in chief that you had been working for the Office of the Prosecutor since the year 2003. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could you indicate whether you had been immediately assigned to the team investigating the events in Macedonia or whether you had been assigned at that time to any other team?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I recall that I began my work with the ICTY, I think on 7 May 2003, and I was immediately assigned to this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that this is the only case -- or is it correct that it's the only case you've been assigned to since those days?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily. I have been working on other cases as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, however, that your primary activity were with this particular team. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would say that activities with this team would take the bulk of my time or at least 50 per cent of my time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've indicated, and I have shown a document to you in evidence already that during that period of time when you worked for the Office of the Prosecutor you prepared a number of summary and analyses. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is exactly in line with my duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall approximately how many reports or memorandum you would have prepared for this particular team, the Macedonian team, Team 7, in relation to your activities?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember how many documents were prepared, but firstly I would like to say that they were not necessarily prepared for the team, as you specifically presenting it. These documents were also for my own consumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that those documents, as I believe you've indicated yesterday, had to do, in part, with the alleged armed conflict but also with the accused or the suspects and you also indicated, I believe, with the events in the village of Ljuboten? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: These documents mostly related to the armed conflict in Macedonia, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it also referred, and perhaps to a lesser extent, you've indicated, but also to the accused or suspects in this case and to the events in the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned previously, I was involved in a number of interviews mostly of military personnel like Mr. Despodov, for instance, and I was essentially provided expert knowledge for the investigator to carry on with his interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And we've seen already from your analysis at least one document that we received from the Office of the Prosecutor that your contribution and your suggestion extended to Mr. Boskoski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I explained previously, one of my functions as a member of the military analysis unit is to place officials under investigation into the context of crimes or context of events related to armed conflicts.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I think you've indicated, Mr. Bezruchenko, that you can't remember how many memos or summaries you have produced and that's only normal. But can you remember approximately how many there would have been. Would we talking of half a dozen, a dozen, several dozens, are you able to say?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps a dozen.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And -- and that would cover the time from 2003 up to these days. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that -- or are you aware that in the month of May of 2005 the Defence of Mr. Boskoski challenged the jurisdiction of this Tribunal on the basis that there had been no armed conflict in Macedonia in 2001. Is that a fact that you are aware of?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall this fact, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that as a result, the Office of the Prosecutor decided that it would be necessary for the case to find a -- an expert that could possibly give evidence about this matter. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't really know if there existed any direct link between these two events as you described them. I just cannot comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, are you aware of the fact that the Office of the Prosecutor sought to identify a potential expert that could give evidence about the issue of an alleged armed conflict in Macedonia in the year 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if this was the case, I was not aware of it. At least, well, I was not really in the picture of what was going on in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall that in fact, Mr. Bezruchenko, you and other individuals from the Office of the Prosecutor interviewed a man called Steven Sulejman Schwartz. Do you recall that interview?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it was a formal interview. We just had a very brief meeting with this person.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you recall meeting with that person, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall what the purpose of that meeting was?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think -- I think that there was an idea of involving him as a military -- no, sorry, not military. He would not really have any military background. As a political expert for this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that this person was introduced to you as a expert who had written extensively about the region?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But is it correct that this is the way the person had been introduced to you prior to the meeting?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not really. I don't think so. In any case, I didn't really come across his name as a source of any major publication about Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall what the position of Mr. Schwartz was about the alleged existence of an armed conflict in the Republic of Macedonia at the time?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really. I only know that Mr. Schwartz is now in Bosnia and he is serving as one of major advisors on the political issues of Islam to [indiscernible] Sulejman in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall what the position of Mr. Schwartz was in relation to the structure and functioning of the NLA, the National Liberation Army?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I can assist you there. I will show you what is Rule 65 ter 1D864. Mr. Bezruchenko, what will appear in front of you is an investigator's notes prepared by -- well, by the Office of the Prosecutor and the meeting took place on the 24th of August of 2005, and as investigators, the names of those conducting the interviews are Deidra Sampson, Viktor Bezruchenko and Rafael La Cruz. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can, but I would like to say again that in fact I don't really think this was a formal interview. We simply had lunch with this person, and we had a brief discussion with him about what he knows about Macedonia, and he basically can't really produce any significant knowledge on the conflict. He failed in fact to mention the most fundamental names of individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's look first perhaps, Mr. Bezruchenko, at the first subheading in that document, which is the purpose of the interview. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will read it out to you. It says this: "Steven Schwartz was introduced to the team as an authority on Bosnian Mujahedins and also has a very good knowledge, and also has a very good knowledge of the conflicts in Kosovo and Macedonia. He is a journalist and has authored publications on the Balkan conflict." And then it says: "In a cursory meeting with the team including trial attorney Bill Smith and team leader Harit Sandhu, it was put forward to Mr. Schwartz that we are seeking an expert witness with a good general background knowledge of Macedonia during and around the period of the conflict in 2001. Mr. Schwartz presented that he may be that person and agreed to a more detailed interview from which we can draw an assessment of his knowledge." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that. I think that perhaps the key word in this particular paragraph is "cursory," which again confirms my view that it was a very brief meeting, and I didn't really get an impression from this meeting that Mr. Schwartz, despite his time in Bosnia, either spoke any of the languages spoken in the area or had any sufficient military background.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But, Mr. Bezruchenko, the cursory meeting to which the first sentence refers to refers not to the meeting which you had, but a meeting between Mr. Smith, Mr. Sandhu and the witness. If you look at the last sentence the way in which your meeting is referred to is as a more detailed interview. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this on the next page?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No. It's the last sentence of the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you scroll down this document, please. I can see that the last paragraph on this page is, "Further videos can be found in his CV which is attached."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No. I apologise, Mr. Bezruchenko. If you can go back up the page and remain within the subheading "purpose of interview," and if you go to the second paragraph which starts with the word "in a cursory meeting." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you agree that the cursory meeting which is being referred to here is a meeting including trial attorney Bill Smith and team leader Harit Sandhu. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the last sentence in that paragraph it says that Mr. Schwartz presented that he may be that person and agreed to a more detailed interview from which we can draw an assessment of his knowledge. So do you agree that the more detailed interview is in fact what comes next in this document?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apparently so. That's right. I remember that he was saying that he could be the person who could be contacted on the issues related to conflict in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that the next words that follows is the word "the interview." Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the registry please turn to the next page, please. And you can see that he -- he was asked, among other things, about Mr. Boskoski, about structures, and about the NLA on this page. Do you agree with that? Perhaps can you scroll down a bit for the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can focus on the bottom of the page, about his knowledge of the NLA. I would like to read to you what is noted there: "Schwartz has had no personal contact with the NLA but has had contacts with persons close to the NLA. He has a basic knowledge of the formation of the UCK MP and the evolution of the NLA which he called -- which he calls the second UCK. He does not believe the NLA is a outgrowth of the KLA." And then he told you this: "He does not see the point of the NLA, believes the group was provocative, adventurous and unnecessary. He considers them an opportunistic bunch of persons who became," and if we can turn to the next page, "who became violent when they began to be taken on by the Macedonian security forces." And he adds that "The structure was not well organised like the KLA, created quickly and improvised." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you now recall Mr. Schwartz telling you this?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. We had lunch basically with this person, as I mentioned, and we were talking during the lunch and he was telling us all these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will agree that, should this information have been accepted or presented by you, this would have been a rather, let's say, difficult type of evidence, and by that I mean that it directly contradicts the case which you are trying to present to this Chamber. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all I would like to correct a mistake in the statement it not UCP MP. It is UCP MB, which stands for liberation army of Presevo, Medvedja and Bujanovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful for that, Mr. Bezruchenko. Would you be able to answer the previous question? And if you wish, I can --

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- put it to you again.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My impression was that Mr. Schwartz in reality had pretty limited opinion of what was going in Macedonia and which was basically taken from various international media. I don't really think that he spoke to any sufficient degree any of the languages spoken in the area, be it B/C/S or Macedonian. The other point which sort of struck me about Mr. Schwartz was that he didn't really have any relevant qualifications in terms of military knowledge to make any judgment about the military organisations.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that your office, Mr. Bezruchenko, took the decision not to call Mr. Schwartz as an expert. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware if this decision was taken or if there was any specific person who made this decision. But apparently the services which Mr. Schwartz offered were not accepted.
