utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree also, coming closer to you this time, do you agree that you made no reference to the information provided to you by Mr. Schwartz during this interview in your report. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, in a sense this is information did not really differ very much from numerous media articles which appeared on the subject in Macedonia. Well, I didn't really find anything new in this information, no facts, no exact knowledge, no specific date.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in answer to my question, you did not refer to that particular document in your report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask to look now at the bottom of the page, that's page 1D -- yes, thank you. It is the correct page. You will see there's a section of the document which is referred to as "interviewer's comments." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There are some comments here.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can draw your attention in particular to the very last paragraph on that interviewer's comments, and I will read it out to you. The interviewers said this: "My concerns about using him as an expert witness are, 1, he was never in Macedonia for an extended period and was not there during the conflict. His contacts were limited local Albanians, not officials and not Slav Macedonians. He is not an academic expert on the area." So you would agree that this is essentially the basis or the reason why at the time it was considered that Mr. Schwartz was an inadequate choice as an expert witness. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what appear from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I may ask you this: Is that correct that in the crisis period in 2001 you were not personally in the Republic of Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in fact you were I believe - and correct me if I'm wrong - working and studying in Sarajevo at the time, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was in Bosnia then.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I don't mean that as a criticism, Mr. Bezruchenko, but you will agree that are not an academic expert on the area, either? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not academic expert, no.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the speakers not to overlap. It is for our sake and for the transcript's sake.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise for the absence of breaks during the questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that the knowledge which you have acquired about the functioning and the structure of the Macedonian authorities and the relevant documentation which you have reviewed to acquire that knowledge was acquired as a result and as part of your work as a military analyst for the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And prior to that time, had you no particular contacts with the Macedonian authorities in the region -- or the Macedonian authorities or the representative of those authorities is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at that time, no, I didn't have.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could we please turn to the next page of that document, and if we can go to the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There's another paragraph. It says this: "Mr. Schwartz' contacts are limited to journalists and person at the local level who could be used as leads for more qualified information on Macedonia. As such, we suggest that he can be used as an alternative if other leads do not prove to be successful." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware, Mr. Bezruchenko, of any other interviews or interview of potential candidates by the Prosecution to try to identify a expert who could give evidence about the matters which have been touched with Mr. Schwartz, in particular the NLA and the conflict?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, I don't think that we contacted anyone else. At least I was not really involved in any interviews in relation to these specific persons. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that in your report and again in court you have referred to a particular book known in English as War in Macedonia. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the book by Mr. Damjanovski and Kuzov?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I used this book.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you interview any of the three authors of this book which you called experts? Did you interview any of those three people, to your knowledge, this is?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, unfortunately not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that within a couple of months of the interview with Mr. Schwartz, you had become the listed Prosecutor expert on its Rule 65 ter list. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand, sir, what you mean by have become a expert. Well, yes, my name was put on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that the decision to select you as an expert to appear and to give evidence on behalf of the Prosecutor was taken at some stage during the 24th of August of 2005 and the 7th of November of 2005. Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I'm only aware of the fact that I was asked to prepare my report and that I might be possibly asked to provide evidence in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall, Mr. Bezruchenko, when you were first asked by the Office of the Prosecutor to prepare this report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember exactly because several years have passed already, but I think it was either in 2004 or 2005, probably end of 2004 or maybe 2005.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This question and the answer were covered in the last session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that even after the time when you had been asked to become an expert for the Prosecutor, you continued to provide advice and assistance to the Prosecution team?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In which sense, Mr. Mettraux?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, for instance, that you were consulted by colleagues of yours from the Office of the Prosecutor in relation to particular witnesses, first?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: To particular documents, first of all, I was asked to interpreter this or that document, in fact. Well, regarding the witnesses, I'm not certain, really. I think at some point in time I stopped being involved at working with witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that even during pre-trial and in the trial you were asked for -- to provide your expertise in relation to a number of documents which were to be used at trial by the Office of the Prosecutor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really. In fact, after my report was completed, I almost had no opportunity to comment on this or that document, because by and large, the report was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that you were consulted in particular in relation to a filing made by the Office of the Prosecution where the Prosecution sought to tender a number of document, that they be admitted by the Trial Chamber and you were asked by counsel what the relevance and importance of those documents were?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you kindly qualify your question, Mr. Mettraux, which documents you are referring to and what is the approximate date of the filing?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The documents in question, Mr. Bezruchenko, are documents which appeared at the time on the Rule 65 ter list of the Prosecution and for which the Prosecution made an application for admission. I do not have the exact number of the Rule 65 ter in front of me and I will seek to find it for you later today, and the filing was made, I believe, earlier this year. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't, Mr. Mettraux. I say again if you specifically indicate to me which document you are referring to, I might be in a position to help you. Otherwise, I'm afraid not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In that case I will come back to you with the information, Mr. Bezruchenko. Is it correct that a lot of the information which you used to prepare your report had in fact been contained in the various reports and memorandums which you had prepared for the Office of the Prosecutor at an earlier stage. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really. I am afraid you're overestimating the role of the memos and memorandums, because they were not initially intended to be the basis for my report. In fact, the work in earnest of the report began quite late when I was directly asked to prepare this report. Otherwise, these documents were prepared in reference to interpretation of various documents like the book by Mr. Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that at the time when the Prosecution asked you to become the expert in this case, they would have been fully aware of what your position was in relation to the matter which you were asked to provide expert evidence upon. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot really tell what kind of judgment my colleagues or any persons who would be involved in this matter would make about my views. It was entirely undiscrete matter for them only, but I would say that by the time I began doing my report, from my research, from Internet, from numerous media materials, as well as from some documents, I had already some basic, but not conclusive ideas about the conflict in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct however, Mr. Bezruchenko, that at the time when the Prosecution asked you to become the expert in this case, they would have known from you that you held the view that there had been a conflict in Macedonia in 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is not really a public secret, Mr. Mettraux, that this conflict did take place. I'm not the only expert, or, rather, I'm not really the only person who has been dealing with this issue who maintained this point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But simply to answer my question, Mr. Bezruchenko, and I will repeat it, is it correct that at the time when the Prosecution asked you to become the expert in this case, they would have known from you that you held the view that there had been a conflict in Macedonia in 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really. I don't think that I made a particular point of bragging about my knowledge of the conflict in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, did you perhaps tell them that, in your view, there had been a conflict in Macedonia in 2001 during discussions or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think both my colleagues and I were reading numerous international reports and media reports which actually related to what happened in Macedonia in 2001 as conflict. So I simply think there is no other word to describe it but the word "conflict."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: May I take your answer, Mr. Bezruchenko, as an agreement that in fact you had made your position quite clear to your colleagues that, in your view, there had been a conflict in Macedonia in 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the implication of your question, Mr. Mettraux, is that I was specifically expressed the views that a conflict in Macedonia as described in legal terms was taking place in Macedonia in 2001, this was not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you make your position clear as regard your field of expertise, the military analysis that, in your view, and according to the doctrine of military expertise, there was a conflict in Macedonia in 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not really understand your question, Mr. Mettraux. What actually do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I will ask you the question again. Is it correct that at the time when the Prosecution asked you to become the expert in this case they would have known from you that you held the view that there had been a conflict in Macedonia in 2001, and I will specify according to your military understanding of that term. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think they specifically knew it from me. As I say it was not a public secret; it was open knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D724, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, that is, again, your summary and analysis of Mr. Boskoski's book and I will ask the registry to turn to page 17, please. That is 1D00-6427. And if you can scroll down a little bit to the paragraph numbered 1. Thank you. Mr. Bezruchenko, if can you focus again on paragraph 1 of your analysis, you said this: "Boskoski's views were formed under the strong influence of radical Macedonian disguised as patriotism, he espouses strong nationalist idealogies -- idealogy." And then it says: "Boskoski's uncompromising support for the military option during the conflict." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what you referring there to is a conflict according to your understanding of this term in military doctrine. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I may turn to the next page, please. If we can go to the top of that page, please. Thank you. In paragraph 3 you said and you referred to "throughout the Albanian-Macedonian conflict." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And again that would be a reference to your military understanding of this notion. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you would agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that at least as early as 24th of April of 2004 and you've indicated that was prior to the time when you were asked to become an expert by the Prosecution, the Office of the Prosecutor would have been fully aware that you held the view that, according to the doctrine or the military doctrine, you took the view that there was and had been a conflict in Macedonia in 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may explain it in the following way, Mr. Mettraux. There was indeed a conflict in military understanding of this term going on in Macedonia in 2001. Or in fact it was following this conflict even when I was in Bosnia as soon as this conflict began, because it was extremely interesting to follow what was happening and it was definitely an extension of other conflicts in the, as I would describe, political space of the former Yugoslavia. Well, on the other hand, the implication of the question whether my colleagues knew only from me and exclusively from me that there was a conflict going on, then your assertion is completely wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Bezruchenko, if you understood my question to have that suggestion built in it. It was a question that related to your position and whether you had made that position known to them, your position, so you would agree if I rephrase it, that you made your personal position quite clear to your colleagues at least in this document. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is based on the analysis of the book which was produced by Mr. Boskoski. And I think, I think he uses the same words in describing the events in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that, Mr. Bezruchenko. I will ask you this about your report. Could you indicate who, if anyone, assisted you in locating and identifying material which you believed to be relevant to preparing your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is your answer to be understood as suggesting that all of the material which is referred to in your expert report was in fact identified and selected by yourself?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the way it worked was like this. Part of the material was found in the open sources, like media, I was specifically studying various Macedonian newspapers and magazines relating to the period of the conflict. A lot of material was also derived from various international sources which were open sources again, and finally, whenever I felt there was a specific need to fill in certain gaps in the analysis, which unfortunately happens now and then, well, I would describe what kind of documents I would need, and my colleagues and I would come up with specific RFAs, that is request for assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So if I understand, and I wish to understand your answer clearly, Mr. Bezruchenko. The responsibility to locate or to identify material that would be or could be relevant to the preparation of your report was your responsibility. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say by and large, yes, but not entirely. Unfortunately, unfortunately, I could not get the full access to the Macedonian military archives.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps to understand when you say "not entirely," is your qualification of the answer limited to the fact that on some occasions access to certain document had to be obtained from third parties. Is that the only qualification you make to your answer?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please qualify your answer -- your question, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, I simply want to be clear on the qualification which you gave to my question. You have said, "I would say by and large, yes, but not entirely." That was the question whether you were the one with the responsibility to select and locate and identify the material. And then you said unfortunately, you did not have full access to the Macedonian military archives. My follow-up question was whether the limitation which you've mentioned in your answer as to who was responsible to locate and identify material was limited to the difficulties which you had to have full access to military archives or whether there were other factors relevant.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no answer for this question. I think we were all under pressure. There were various tasks facing us and basically there were other priorities. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps you could indicate whether any other members of the team of the Office of the Prosecutor assisted you in locating and identifying material which would be or could be relevant to the preparation of your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Mr. Thomas Keuhnel, the investigator on a number of occasions provided some documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did anyone else assisted you in your task to prepare a report from the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not really in -- if you mean the writing the actual report and the analysis, certainly assistance was provided, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What about the identification and location of document; in addition to Mr. Kuehnel, did anyone else provide you or suggested document that would be or could be relevant to the preparation of your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think some documents were provided through witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And any other members of the Prosecution team, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to the best of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that the mandate or the task which you were given or the scope, I should say of the task which you were given to prepare your report changed slightly over time? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not really.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, do you agree, for instance, that in the original request which was made of you there was no request to provide a so-called, I think you called it military chronology of the events in the village Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think that such a thing as military chronology of events in the village ever existed. Well, if you are specifically referring to my section of the report which deals with the events in Ljuboten, this was compounded on the basis of numerous document, but I don't really think that there is something which can be described collectively as military chronology of events in the village ever existed in Macedonia archives. I doubt it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Bezruchenko. I didn't wish to ask you about where that chronology was. I was asking indeed, as you correctly identified, to the part of your report on the event of Ljuboten. Is that correct that this particular part of your report was requested of you at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we have been made -- we have made a number of requests for various documents and they were all, not necessarily all, of course, but well, we received the replies at various points of time. Some were pretty late. Some were received pretty early.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And simply for the record, is it correct that you refer to that part of your report as a military chronology -- I am sorry, military integrated events? Is that the way you described them in the village of Ljuboten on 10, 11 and 12 August 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps if you could specifically indicate the page and paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. That would be paragraph 21, Mr. Bezruchenko, at page 4. It says section 4 presents a narrative of the military integrated events in the village of Ljuboten on 10, 11 and 12 August of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And simply to be clear on this point. Is it correct that the original request which was made of you to prepare a report did not include a narrative of military integrated events as occurred in the village of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, I'm afraid you're asking me something which doesn't exist. Well, I don't really think that, as I mentioned previously, there exists any document which could be described as a narrative of military integrated events which occurred in the village of Ljuboten. Let me repeat again. This section of my report was based on a number of documents, quite a big number of documents, which had to be properly analysed and put in the proper context.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown exhibit P466, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, that's your report again. And I will ask the registry to turn to page 4, please, of that report. It would be a few -- yes. Thank you very much. If you could focus, please, on the top of the page, please.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you look at paragraph 21 of your report, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you see that you refer to section 4 of your report as a narrative of military integrated events in the village of Ljuboten on 10, 11 and 12 August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that. But you probably missed my point, Mr. Mettraux. What I was saying was that I never requested from Macedonian authorities anything which might be described as a single comprehensive narrative of military integrated events in the village of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that specification, Mr. Bezruchenko, but my question was this. Is it correct that over the course of time the scope of the expertise which was asked of you changed?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In which sense, Mr. Mettraux?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that at some stage during the preparation of your report you were asked by the Office of the Prosecutor to add certain parts of your reports -- or add parts to your report, I should say.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had a plan. We had a discussion of this plan with my colleagues and it was adopted with minor changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And when you refer to the plan that you discussed with your colleagues, that would be your colleagues of the Office of the Prosecutor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was Mr. -- I think I referred to these persons in my report on the very first page. This was Mr. Dan Saxon and Bill Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that -- or I should ask you this. Is it correct that one of the part of the report which was asked of you at a later date not in the original request was this narrative of military integrated events in the village of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that was probably something which was a part of the original plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that one of the aspects of your report which was later asked of you or asked of you to add to your report was the part of the report which relates to the alleged disciplinary responsibilities within the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this then. Is it correct that on 7 of November of 2005 when the Prosecution provided for the first time the list of proposed witnesses, in addition to yourself, a person was proposed as an expert about the functioning and the structure of the Ministry of the Interior, in particular as related to conduct of criminal investigation and disciplinary matters. Do you have a memory of that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't, and honestly speaking, that was not really my concern. My concern was to do the report in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall that the name of that proposed expert at the time was Professor Marijanovic. Can you recall his name?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall that Mr. Marijanovic was -- or the professor in question which was contacted was asked questions about the structure and was approached about the structure and the functioning of the Ministry of Interior. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I ever met Professor Marijanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But are you aware, sir, of the fact that he was approached and asked questions about the structure and functioning of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware perhaps that at the time, Mr. Marijanovic indicated to the Office of the Prosecutor that he could not agree with the nature of the case which the Prosecution was trying to put forth. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I mentioned previously, Mr. Mettraux, I never had a chance to talk to Mr. Marijanovic. I never met him and I don't know what he might have told to my colleagues or anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, however, that as a result, you were asked to increase the scope of your report by adding several parts of material pertaining to the Ministry of the Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so, because at the very start, my task was to describe the two major components of the security forces of Macedonia which is the army and the Ministry of Interior, and of course this task cannot be really approached in a cohesive and regular manner without describing the legislation pertaining to the Ministry of Interior as well as its structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And just so that the record is clear on this point, Mr. Bezruchenko, is it correct that you have never worked for the Ministry of Interior of Macedonia Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never worked for the Ministry of Interior of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you never lectured or published any article concerning the structure and functioning of the Ministry of Interior of Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And as you've indicated earlier in your evidence your knowledge of the functioning and the structure of the Ministry of Interior was acquired as part of your work for the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like now to turn to a slightly or in fact a completely different issue, Mr. Bezruchenko, and it relate to your discussion in your report of the president of the Republic of Macedonia. Do you recall giving or making statements and comments in your report about the president of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was describing the various powers in relation to the president of the Republic of Macedonia, mostly, I think, as his role as commander in chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will recall, simply to refresh your memory, Mr. Bezruchenko, do you recall that during your examination in chief you were also asked by Mr. Saxon to comment upon a number of orders and decisions which had been signed by the president of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, simply for the record, this would be tab 10 to 25 of the OTP binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that the section which deals with the president of the Republic of Macedonia in your report, Mr. Bezruchenko, is to be found at paragraph 32 and more specifically at section 3.2.3.1; is that correct? And perhaps I should assist you in locating the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the registry can please bring up page 66 of that document, please, that is on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that this particular section of the report which is located under number 3.2.3.1 is the part of your report that deals with the role of the president. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct also that this particular section of the report deals with the Macedonian army generally. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it also correct that you did not deal with the powers of the president in relation to the forces of the Ministry of the Interior in your report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think I just provided the description of the basic legislation related to the defence system.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But in the section that deals with the Ministry of Interior do you agree that there is no section relevant to the role of the president. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not really.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sorry, just to clarify your answer, Mr. Bezruchenko. Are you suggesting that you devoted a section or a part of your report dealing with the Ministry of Interior to the powers and responsibility of the president.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm suggest is that the role of the president is, to my mind, adequately described under paragraph 3.2.3.1 and there was no real need to carry on with any other descriptions in the part of the report dealing with the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the registry could turn to page 69, please. I believe it would be the next page, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that -- Mr. Bezruchenko, that is the part of the report that deals with the role of the government. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this page 67, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: 69, please, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that this is the part of your report that deals with the role of the government. Is that --

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And again, this is the same part of your report that deals generally with the army, ARM, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because this is the part of my report in which I'm describing the general system of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that in the part that deals with the forces of the Ministry of Interior you have not dealt with the role of the government in a distinct section. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not, because I don't think it was really necessary, since, as I say, the role of the government is described in paragraph 3.2.3.3.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would like to ask you a few general question which may be of relevance here, Mr. Bezruchenko, about the issues of terminology. You would agree that generally in military matters a proper use of term is an important matter. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it is equally important for you to use the proper terms when using them in your report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree that the concept or the notion of order in military doctrine has a particular significance or a particular meaning. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps I should show you a document that I have shown you already in the past. This would be Rule 65 ter 1D928. Mr. Bezruchenko, that's, again, the department of defence dictionary of military and associated terms that we have seen before. And I ask the registry please to turn to page 396. It is at 1D00-7884, please. And if the registry could please scroll down a little bit on this page and focus on the middle of the page. Thank you. Mr. Bezruchenko, can you locate the entry under the title "order?" Can you see that entry?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the -- the lexicon defines it in the following term: "A communication, written, oral or by signal which conveys instructions from a superior to a subordinate. In a broad sense the terms order and command are synonymous. However, an order implies discretion as to the details of execution, whereas a command does not." Do you agree with that definition that it's a generally authoritative definition in the military field. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that this definition is generally authoritative. However, I would say that this definition may be limited to specific cultural differences and application in specific armed forces. And as a general comment I would like to ask you, Mr. Mettraux, which particular document related to the Ministry of Interior or Ministry of Defence that you're applying this definition to?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, there is a number of documents, Mr. Bezruchenko, that I will kindly ask you later to comment upon. At this stage I would like to ask you this. Is it correct that in military doctrine the concept of order is different from, for instance, the concept of decision?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is normally different.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Mr. Bezruchenko, I will apologise to you, but I will provide you with the page which contains the definition of the dictionary, the same dictionary. It has not been uploaded by my own fault, by the definition it gives is as follows. It says: "An estimate of the situation, a clear and concise statement of the line of action intended to be followed by the commander as the one most favourable to the successful accomplishment of the assigned mission"?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see it on the screen, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No, Mr. Bezruchenko, unfortunately by my own fault, you won't be able to see it today, so what I will simply do is to ask you whether the definition that I have given you would be a pretty accurate expression of what you understood to be a decision in military terms?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily as applied in the Macedonian army, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you suggesting, Mr. Bezruchenko, that the definition of orders or decisions as defined in the military doctrine of the United States would vary from those which you say were used in the Macedonian army?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you understand them to be different or is it simply a possibility that you are raising?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is simply a possibility, because I would say that in fact as you are well aware, Macedonian army had a very rich cultural and historical heritage from the JNA, and therefore it had its own traditions and its own ways of command and control related to decisions and implementing these decisions and orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, with the suggestion that it would be pretty relevant to determine the exact nature or the purport of a particular document to establish whether it was an order or a decision?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in general terms only [Realtime transcript read in error "horizontally"].

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would also agree that it would be relevant, for instance, to know the nature of the authority which was exercised by the person rendering the order for the decision. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I don't quite understand what you mean by "horizonitally."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I didn't think I made a reference to "horizontally." I'm -- I apologise, Mr. Bezruchenko. Would you agree that the term that would be used in a particular document might or could be relevant to determine the nature of the authority which was exercised by the person which adopted or signed the document in question? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What -- if I may ask you, sir, what do you actually mean by nature of authority?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you that way. Would you agree that the type of authority or the extent of authority which is exercised by a person when he or she issues an order as opposed to a decision or another form of documentation of that sort, could be different. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, again, I have to ask to you -- I'm sorry, I'm really sorry, but I have to ask you to you qualify your question. Are you specifically referring to technical authority, are you specifically referring an extent of authority? You are simply mixing up these two things.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Bezruchenko. The record didn't pick up the word which you said was being mixed up. The record said "are you referring to a" and then "mixed up two things."

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What I was trying to say was that you appear to be mixing up two things in the same question. First you are saying it is type of authority. Then you add "or" and say extent of authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Very well. Then I will ask you first about the type of authority. Would you agree that the type or that the nature of the document in question that is being exercised in a document could vary or could be indicated by the terms or the name of the particular document? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are various sorts of orders, of course. There are administrative orders, there are logistical orders, there are warning orders, there are [indiscernible] orders, there are operational orders. There are various orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree that the type [Realtime transcript read in error "time"] of authority could vary between, say, an order on the one hand and a decision on the other. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, with all my due respect, Mr. Mettraux, I will have to ask you again, what do you actually mean by the type of authority and again I must note it appears that the record is not really entirely correct. It says "time of authority," not "type of authority," if I understand you correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, based on the two definitions that I have read to you, Mr. Bezruchenko, of what constitute a decision or an order according to the military doctrine, would you agree with that proposition that the nature of the authority which is being exercised is different in one case and in the other. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would counsel and witness please slow down their exchange.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot really agree do it, because I don't really understand what you mean, sir. If you are specifically referring to a interrelation between an order and a decision, normally at least in the military terms, order is based on a decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well I'm grateful for that, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient time, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux. We resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And perhaps an indication at the start of this session, it may be hard to believe, but it seems that we have gone faster than was foreseen in relation to several parts of questioning of Mr. Bezruchenko and the Defence shed in light of Mr. Bezruchenko's evidence a good part of its questions. As a result of it, Your Honour, we believe that the Defence may have to ask for a shorter session during this session which may perhaps speed things up when we restart this witness rather than slow -- slow things down, we believe it may be more efficient, but for the time being I will simply try to move forward until the point where -- which we reach where it may become better to interrupt rather than continue. Obviously, with the leave of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, I apologise for the delay. Is it correct that the president of Macedonia, the president of the republic, Mr. Trajkovski was legally competent to issue orders to his subordinates. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct --

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that in your examination in chief you were in fact shown a number of documents by Mr. Saxon which specifically referred to the document being an order with a reference to "I order" as signed by the president; is that correct, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen a number of such documents, I think for the most part, and the proper translation for these documents would be decision. In fact they were mostly decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, do you agree that perhaps with this. Is it correct that a number of the documents which you were shown were decisions whereas some others were in fact orders. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I may ask you to look at your report once again, Mr. Bezruchenko. That would be page 67 of your report. That's exhibit P466, please. And I'll ask you, Mr. Bezruchenko, to focus particularly on paragraph 251 of your report and the following. Is it correct that in paragraph 251 to 257 of your report you refer to a number of decisions issued by President Trajkovski? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree also that you were shown a number of documents by the Prosecution which referred to the expression "orders" during your examination in chief? Do you recall those?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I recall those documents, but I cannot really tell at this point of time which of those were actually decisions and which of those were actually orders, but, yes, I remember those documents, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps to expedite matter, Your Honour, we will come back on a number of those documents but those referred to as orders shown to Mr. Bezruchenko are exhibit P472, P476, P477, P478, Exhibit 1D100 and exhibit P479 and they are in the binder of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that the use of the expression "order" in relation to documents signed by the president of Macedonia is not a random matter but one that depends on the legal basis which is being used to sign a particular document. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think really that in legal terms, so I am probably not really in a position to comment on that. But if you are looking for my view on this matter I would probably comment by saying that there is not really serious difference in terms of a decision and order in the legal term, since both types of documents convey the same idea. That is, the will of the president to carry out a certain action.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that when the legal basis for the document was Article 15, 11 of the Law of Defence and that would be the old law, Mr. Bezruchenko, the document would be named and it would be legally considered to be a decision. Are you aware of this fact?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, simply for the record this would be tab 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 and 21 of the OTP binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that when the legal basis used or in relation to which the president signed a document was Article 15, 10 of the Law on Defence, the old law, the document in question would be characterised as an order. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not certain about this point. Because essentially I was really concentrating on the analysing of the Law on Defence which was passed in June 2001 which was more pertinent in fact and more comprehensive in a sense of addressing military matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I'll simply ask you to confirm this then.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown exhibit P476, please. That would be at tab 18 of the Prosecution binder, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, we will come back on a number of these documents together. But at this stage I would simply ask to you look at the preamble of this document signed by Mr. Boris Trajkovski, president of the Republic of Macedonia. It's dated the 7th of June of 2001. Is it correct that in the preamble the legal basis referred to in relation to this document is Article 79, paragraph 2 of the constitution and Article 15, item 10 of the Law on Defence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next document in the Prosecution binder, tap 19. And it's exhibit P477, please. And again I'll simply ask to you look at the preamble for the time being on this document, Mr. Bezruchenko. Do you agree that this is again an order signed by the president, Mr. Trajkovski? This one is dated the 8th of June 2001 and the legal basis for this document is again Article 79, paragraph 2 of the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia and Article 15, item 10 of the Law on Defence. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps to show you another one. It's exhibit P478, please. It is in tab 20 of the Prosecution binder. And while it shows up on the screen, Mr. Bezruchenko, can you recall at this stage that the Article in question had to do with the mobilisation of the army or is it something beyond your memory?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which specific Article are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise. It's Article 15, item 10. Can you recall what it related to?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this is the new law or is it the old law?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It's the old law, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, obviously the Article - and this is my assumption - is related to mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that. And you agree that the preamble again of this order is Article 79, paragraph 2 of the constitution and Article 15, item 10 of the Law on Defence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. And as far as I recall, Article 79 actually stipulates the powers of the president as his role of the commander in chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that. And I will ask you a couple of questions about this afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, simply for the completeness of the record, I would also direct the Chamber's attention to Exhibit 1D100 which is tab 22 of the Prosecution binder and exhibit 479 which is tab 23 of the Prosecution binder. And I'll ask the registry to please go back to the report of Mr. Bezruchenko. That would be exhibit P466, please. And in particular, at page 111, please. 107; I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this is a paragraph that we've seen already a couple of times. And at paragraph 371 of your report you say this: "Several Macedonian Ministry of Interior documents suggest that minister of interior Boskoski exercised operational control of police forces which was manifested in orders to deploy police at various crisis areas." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, can I.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would you agree that you then refer to 29 -- I believe 29 different telegrams and in all but two of them you suggest that those are orders or at least that they are ordering certain matters. Well, first I should perhaps ask you this perhaps. Is it correct that you sought to represent in your report these 29 telegrams as orders from Mr. Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, if you assume that the definition of an order which you have just provided me as taken from the dictionary of military terms is correct, and I would like to remind you that this definition speaks of an order as conveying specific instructions, then, I think I had sufficient grounds to interpret these telegrams in fact as orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that in only two cases of those telegrams, you have referred to them as authorising something. Is it correct? That's at paragraph 372 and 374 of your report. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, however, Mr. Bezruchenko, that none of those documents which you have characterised as orders in your report actually bear that title. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you're right. I think the proper title is a telegram, but I think I mention it in my report as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct also that in none of them is the injunction or the word to order something used by the minister? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps you could come back to one of those orders and take a look at them again?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. Bezruchenko. If we can turn perhaps randomly to exhibit P468, that would be, if you have the binder, Mr. Bezruchenko, tab 6 of the Prosecution binder.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreters kindly ask you once again to avoid overlapping.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I take a look at the Macedonian copy as well, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Certainly. I have a paper copy, Mr. Bezruchenko. I think the Macedonian version is at the back of the English in your binder.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher there is -- it is apparently on the screen, Mr. Bezruchenko, but I will give you the --

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is fine if it is on the screen already. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you can you confirm at least as far as this particular document is concerned that Mr. Boskoski or first that the document does not bear the title of an order. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't bear this title. It clearly bears the title of telegram.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree also that Mr. Boskoski or the person who prepared the order on his behalf did not use the term or the expression ordering or "I order," do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct also that what this document or the phrasing of this document is in fact quite different. In the second line of that document, if you can see, it says that it is needed that certain things happen. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are various ways of expressing it in English. I would rather say for the sake of security measures, 50 policemen will be. But you can also translate it this way as needed. But to be more precise I would rather say "will be."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that in the next paragraph it says the policemen should be equipped. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Should be or will be.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in the last sentence of that second paragraph, the expression which is used and again in the last paragraph of that document is Mr. Boskoski asking things. He asked to take hand radio and asked to conduct. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir. Say it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. If you can locate the last sentence in the second paragraph of the text of the order, as you call it, it uses the phrase "the senior officers are asked to take hand radio link equipment." Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think what it really says is that the commanders will carry the hand-held radio, reserve batteries and the charger.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But if you look at the English translation of this document, Mr. Bezruchenko, do you agree that the way it has been translated by CLSS is that what in fact the minister of the interior is doing is to ask a number of things. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see in the sentence the word "ask," sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if you look at the English translation perhaps, Mr. Bezruchenko, which is on your screen, I believe, as well, there is a-- the last sentence of the second paragraph uses the expression "the senior officer are asked," and then in the last sentence there is the phrase "the senior officers before the departures of the unit are asked." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that, sir, but what I'm say something is that this word is indeed in the English translation of this document, but I don't really see this word in the Macedonian copy of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will agree as well, Mr. Bezruchenko, that this document as well as the other telegrams to which you have referred to in your report do not refer to any particular legal basis on which this particular telegram was prepared or issued. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't seem to mention any particular clauses of the Law on Internal Affairs or any other document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps it is a obvious question, Mr. Bezruchenko, but do you agree that from this document it cannot be determined whether prior to this telegram being sent there had been discussions and an agreement between, on the one hand the Ministry of Interior and perhaps Mr. Boskoski himself, and the sector in Kocani. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think the telegram could be sent without any prior warning.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that it could also be sent after discussions or agreement having been reached in relation to this document? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it could be both.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'd like to go back now to your report for a second, Mr. Bezruchenko, and I'll ask you please to turn again to paragraph 3.2.3.1 of your report, and particularly to paragraph 250 of your report, please.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 250, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, please. It's page 66.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that at paragraph 250 of your report you refer to Article 18 of the Law of Defence concerning the functionings and responsibility of the president relating to defence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I think you have clarified the matter already in your previous answer, Mr. Bezruchenko. But is it correct that in addition to this particular provision, the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia also endowed the president with particular competencies or responsibilities as regarded the Armed Forces. Is that correct? And I think you have referred to Article 79 of the constitution.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we're talking about different things here. We are talking about constitution and -- or we're talking about the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me ask the question in that way, sir. Is it correct that in addition to the Law of Defence, and you've specifically referred to Article 18 of that law, the constitution itself, Article 79, in particular 79, paragraph 2 of the constitution, gave some powers to the president of the Republic of Macedonia in relation to the Armed Forces, which are detailed in part in the law itself. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Article 79 of the constitution stipulates that the president of the Republic of Macedonia is in effect commander in chief of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that at some stage or on occasions the president of the Republic of Macedonia would sometime act in relation to those Armed Forces directly on the basis of Article 79 of the constitution, without referring otherwise to the Law of Defence. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was totally within the discretionary powers of the president.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In view of the answer, Your Honour, I will simply refer to exhibit P481 and exhibit 1D52, Your Honour, and I believe the time has been reached to act upon my original warning, Your Honour, if that would be possible, to perhaps take the recess?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You would like now to adjourn with a view to continuing when next the evidence of this witness can continue; is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, and I'm very grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And do we understand that it may be convenient to everybody if the evidence of this witness is further interrupted for Thursday and Friday?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That would certainly be the case of the Defence, Your Honour. We'd be very grateful. But it would depend on Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the Prosecution has told the Defence it will not object to this interruption if it's being done for the convenience of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We're grateful to the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to say, Mr. Bezruchenko, that the proceeding seems to be taking the course that we need to interrupt your evidence yet again, which I know puts an additional strain on you and your memory, and it would seem to be expected that your evidence will continue on Monday of next week.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's perfectly all right, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
